title: Right-derived transformations through an exact input functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and suppose every complex in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ has a K-injective resolution. Here a complex $I$ is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null homotopic. Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and exact (it preserves kernels and cokernels), and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $\beta:F\Rightarrow G\circ E$ be a natural transformation. Write $D(E)$ for termwise $E$ on the derived categories and $(RF,\eta^F),(RG,\eta^G)$ for total right derived functors with their computation units [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Use their canonical signed-shift comparisons and triangulated structures [def-weil-triangulated-category].

There is a unique natural transformation $\tau:RF\Rightarrow RG\circ D(E)$ such that, after the canonical identifications $D(E)Q_{\mathcal A}K=Q_{\mathcal B}(EK)$,
$$\tau_{Q_{\mathcal A}K}\circ\eta^F_K=\eta^G_{EK}\circ Q_{\mathcal C}(\beta_K)$$
for every complex $K$. Given any K-injective resolutions $s:K\to I$ in $\mathcal A$ and $j:EI\to H$ in $\mathcal B$, its component is represented, under the computation isomorphisms $RF(QK)\cong Q(FI)$ and $RG(D(E)QK)\cong Q(GH)$, by
$$FI\xrightarrow{\beta_I}G(EI)\xrightarrow{G(j)}GH.$$
The result is independent of both resolutions and both comparison choices. For every integer $r$, if $s^F_r:RF(-[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(-)[r]$ and $s^{GE}_r:(RG\circ D(E))(-[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RG\circ D(E))(-)[r]$ are the canonical comparisons, then
$$s^{GE}_{r,K}\circ\tau_{K[r]}=(\tau_K)[r]\circ s^F_{r,K}.$$
Consequently its three components on a distinguished triangle give a morphism of the two image triangles, including the connecting arrow. No preservation of K-injective complexes by $E$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing exact termwise functor D(E) and its canonical factorization on complexes and homotopy categories. Mathlib already supplies its signed shifts and triangulated structure.

source.place: Tags 05SE, 070Y and 070K; exact-input assembly by E4.

proof.text: Restrict each chosen computation unit to the full subcategory of K-injectives, where its components are invertible. The K-injective localization q is an equivalence. Regard it as a localization at isomorphisms and descend the shift structure of the inclusion followed by the termwise functor and Qh using Mathlib Functor.commShiftOfLocalization. Its lifting isomorphism is the inverse restricted unit, with the explicit associator. The same isomorphism and Functor.isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso prove exactness of the chosen derived functor. Compatibility of its unit with shifts holds on K-injectives by the lifting formula. For an arbitrary K choose s:K→I, apply naturality of the two sides of the shift equation to s, and cancel the invertible image of s in the target. Apply this to F and G.

source.place: Tags 05SE, 070Y and 070K; exact-input assembly by E4.

proof.text: Form the natural transformation alpha from termwise beta, the G unit, and the inverse exact-input factorization, inserting the associators explicitly. Surjectivity of the universal bijection of the chosen F pair supplies tau. Cancelling the image of the factorization gives exactly IsExactInputDerivedTransformation. Its uniqueness follows from injectivity of the same bijection.

source.place: Tags 05SE, 070Y and 070K; exact-input assembly by E4.

proof.text: Write the computation unit on complexes by whiskering the homotopy unit and the quotient-to-Q identifications. The homotopy unit equation implies its complex version. The computation isomorphism for s has hom RF(Qs) followed by the inverse complex unit at I. Naturality of tau at Qs and the exact-input factorization reduces the two-resolution expression to the complex unit equation at I. Naturality of the G complex unit at j and cancellation of its invertible component at H finish the computation for every s and j. Since all choices compute the unique tau, no separate comparison maps between resolutions are needed.

source.place: Tags 05SE, 070Y and 070K; exact-input assembly by E4.

proof.text: Verify signed-shift compatibility of termwise beta directly in each degree; all comparison components are identities. Pass it to homotopy categories using the quotient factorization isomorphisms. Consequently alpha commutes with shifts. Restrict the unit equation to K-injectives and insert the associator so its target has the composite shift structure on q followed by RF. Cancel the epimorphic restricted F unit to see that tau precomposed with q commutes with shifts. Essential surjectivity of q and naturality extend this equation to every derived object.

source.place: Tags 05SE, 070Y and 070K; exact-input assembly by E4.

proof.text: Construct the triangle morphism with components tau at the three vertices. The first two squares are naturality. The third follows by combining naturality at the connecting arrow with the shift equation for r=1.
